annotations.text:
Designed from 16px up

Every earlier attempt drew a logo and then shrank it, and the tray glyph was whatever survived. This one runs the other way: the mark was designed as an instrument on the 16-pixel grid first, and the large sizes are the same drawing with room to breathe.

That ordering is why it works at both ends. The tray glyph is not a reduction of the logo — it is the logo, at the size it was designed for.

What it shows: the left column is filled to utilization, the right is marked at the pace line. Fill above the mark means ahead of pace, and the gap is the size of the problem.

Still open

Typography and palette were carried over untouched — Chivo and IBM Plex Mono, and the verdict colours already in the app's tokens. Neither was the thing that was failing, but say the word and they are in scope too.

The wordmark is set, not drawn. If the mark holds up, custom-drawing the 'adjent' letterforms to match its grid is the natural next step.
